Title: A Blending Method for Multiscale Valid Time Shifting within an RRFS-like Ensemble-Based Data Assimilation System
Proposed Project Title: Improving National Weather Service Convection Allowing Hazardous Weather Prediction by Using a Cost-Effective Large Background Ensemble in a Regional FV3 Hybrid EnVar Data Assimilation System
Suggested Parent Project: Improving National Weather Service Convection Allowing Hazardous Weather Prediction by Using a Cost-Effective Large Background Ensemble in a Regional FV3 Hybrid EnVar Data Assimilation System
Authors / PI: Nicholas Gasperoni; Xuguang Wang; Tsung-Han Li; Yongming Wang
Brief Abstract: Abstract A new technique for the valid-time-shifting (VTS) method was developed for a multiscale convection-allowing ensemble data assimilation (DA) and forecast system, assimilating hourly mesoscale in situ and storm-scale radar reflectivity observations. In this study, a blending technique is implemented to construct VTS-expanded covariances that address multiple scales of timing uncertainty within one ensemble. Two time-shifting intervals are chosen—a short shifting appropriate for storm-scale DA (30–60 min) and a longer shifting for mesoscale DA (2–3 h). Output from each time shifting is split into small and large scales and then combined using the small scales from the short time shifting and large scales from the long time shifting.
